$comment: Read by the dev-team plugin hooks (guard.mjs / watch.mjs). Patterns are case-insensitive regexes. deny = blocked, ask = the user must confirm. Environments: test = postgres-test (localhost:5433) · development = Neon branch 'development' (backend/.env, APP_ENV=development) · production = Neon branch 'production' (Fly secrets / secrets manager only). See TEAM.md → Hard rules.

bash.message: Port 5005 is the dev backend. Until backend/.env has been switched to the development branch (npm run env:set-dev-db, run by Nave) it talks to the REAL production database. Use the isolated e2e backend on 5006. After the switch this rule can be relaxed to 'ask'.
A Neon connection. Only the DEVELOPMENT branch may be used from here — never production. Confirm which database this command targets.
Only the isolated test DB (localhost:5433) may be opened with a SQL client.

Raw Prisma writes/Studio are blocked: they use whatever backend/.env points at. Use `npm run migrate:new --prefix backend -- <name>` to create a migration, and `npm run migrate:sync --prefix backend` to apply to the test + development DBs. Production changes ONLY through the migrations step of a deploy.
`.env` files hold real secrets (DB URLs, API keys). Do not read or copy them; `.env.example` / `.env.test.example` are fine.
This script moves a database password from the clipboard into backend/.env. Nave runs it himself, in his own terminal.

This touches the REAL production database and needs the production URL, which should never be in this machine's everyday environment. The one-time baseline (`migrate:baseline-prod`) is meant to be run by Nave himself; confirm before running anything like it from here.
Deploy goes to production (the release step applies pending migrations, if any). Only with Nave's explicit go-ahead in this session.
This deletes the postgres-test data volume (test data only, but it also wipes the schema; it is rebuilt from the migrations by `npm run migrate:test --prefix backend`).

files.message: Migrations are history: once one has run in development or production, editing it changes its checksum and the next run stops. Change the schema with a NEW migration (`npm run migrate:new --prefix backend -- <name>`). Editing is fine only for a migration that has not been applied anywhere, or to add the `-- destructive-ok: <reason>` line.

watch.message: Schema changed. Create the migration: `npm run migrate:new --prefix backend -- <snake_case_name>` (diffs the isolated test DB against the schema and writes prisma/migrations/<ts>_<name>/migration.sql). Read the generated SQL and tell Nave in Hebrew what it does to real data — additive changes (new table / optional column) are safe; DROP / SET NOT NULL / TYPE need a data plan (backup, backfill) in the same file and a `-- destructive-ok: <reason>` line, and the release step refuses them without it. Then `npm run migrate:sync --prefix backend` applies it to the test and development DBs. Production gets it at the next deploy.

A migration changed. It is applied to production by the release step of the next deploy, exactly as committed. Check it is the intended SQL and that any destructive statement carries a `-- destructive-ok: <reason>` line with a data plan.

Deploy configuration changed. Keep: `release_command` in backend/fly.toml (runs `scripts/db-migrate.js release` in the new image before it goes live), the prisma/ and scripts/ copies in backend/Dockerfile, and `migrate:check` in deploy.sh — together they apply pending migrations safely and abort the deploy on a failure.
